query: Given a baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEA with a single-phase BCC structure that suffers from high density and insufficient room-temperature ductility compared to literature reports, propose an intervention to introduce a minor alloying element. The intervention must aim to induce a secondary intermetallic phase to form a reticulated network within the matrix to mitigate crack propagation. Specify the expected trade-off in density versus strength-ductility synergy, the operating regime (room temperature compression), and a falsification experiment to distinguish between solid solution hardening and the proposed phase-structure mechanism.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a minor alloying element to a high-entropy alloy with a BCC structure can induce a secondary intermetallic phase to form a reticulated network within the matrix, mitigating crack propagation and improving strength-ductility synergy.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloy with a BCC structure
generation.intervention: Introduction of a minor alloying element
generation.mechanism: Formation of a reticulated network within the matrix
generation.baseline: High-entropy alloy with a BCC structure without the minor alloying element
generation.uncertainty: The effect of the minor alloying element on the formation of the secondary intermetallic phase and the resulting strength-ductility synergy is uncertain.
generation.falsification_experiment: A experiment to test the effect of the minor alloying element on the formation of the secondary intermetallic phase and the resulting strength-ductility synergy, such as a comparison of the microstructure and mechanical properties of the alloy with and without the minor alloying element.

cited_evidence.text:
High-entropy alloys (HEAs) present a new approach of alloying concepts. Whereas conventional alloys usually comprise one major alloying element and minor additions of other alloying elements to improve properties, HEAs consist of at least five elements with close to equimolar composition. For several compositions, the desired formation of solely solid solutions with a face-centred cubic (fcc) or a body-centred cubic (bcc) structure could be achieved [ [1] , [2] , [3] ].

Several groups of HEAs have been intensively investigated. The term compositionally complex alloys (CCAs) was introduced for HEAs with a multiphase microstructure [ [4] ]. Several investigations prove the formation of primarily cubic phases in the alloy AlCoCrCuFeNi and its derivatives [ [5] , [6] , [7] ]. Aluminium strongly influences the microstructure, phase formation and resulting properties. Furthermore, aluminium acts as a stabiliser of bcc solid solutions and can suppress the formation of complex phases [ [8] , [9] , [10] ].
